content_html:
Microfiber cleans well because its fine filaments trap oil and particles, but performance drops when the fibers are coated with softener or exposed to high heat. Washing microfiber separately from lint-producing fabrics helps preserve that pickup ability.

Separate microfiber from lint-heavy cotton

Cotton towels and other fabrics shed fibers that cling to microfiber. Wash microfiber together or with compatible low-lint synthetics so the cloths do not come out coated in lint.

Use detergent without heavy additives

Use a modest detergent dose and skip fabric softener because it coats the filaments and reduces absorbency. If the cloths are used on specific surfaces, also follow product instructions to avoid leaving incompatible residues.

Avoid high heat

Very high temperatures can distort synthetic fibers. Wash and dry within the care-label limits; air drying or low heat is usually sufficient for household microfiber cloths.

Handle contaminated cloths separately

Cloths used with heavy grease, chemicals, or biological contamination should not automatically be mixed with glass or dusting cloths. Follow the label of the product used and discard a cloth if contamination cannot be removed safely.
